$comment: Hackathon assumptions, not operational doctrine. Every threshold here is shown in the UI so a coordinator can argue with it. Edit this file, not the code.
staticSourceBufferNote: A detection is masked when its pixel centre falls inside a known persistent heat source, or within roughly one pixel footprint of it. A 30 m Landsat pixel and a 3 km Meteosat pixel cannot share one radius.

confirmation.credibleDetectionNote: A single polar-orbit pixel graded MEDIUM or better is already a credible fire signature. Without this floor the score only rewarded corroboration, so a real fire seen once by one satellite scored 10 and was filed as noise.

duplicateNote: A duplicate is the SAME sensor re-reporting the SAME pixel, so the radius scales with that sensor's pixel: half a footprint, floored at 60 m. A fixed radius would be wrong in both directions — 375 m collapses adjacent VIIRS pixels of one large fire into a single detection and shrinks the ignition set, while the same 375 m is a fifth of a Meteosat pixel and lets genuine re-reports through.
